items.title: Hope you like rocks, cause we’ve got heaps of f*cking rocks
items.comments:
Went for a trundle up hermit today to see how the alpine is shaping up. Snow line is sitting around 1650m. You can still basically hike up to the campground. I ditched the trail runners after 2.5km of hiking and managed to break some kind of a trail on skins from just below 1800m. Freezing level came up disgustingly high over the weekend, precip was still falling as rain at 2000m in the afternoon. Just under 50cm of snow sitting on the tent pads at Hermit Campground but streams are still running above 2000m. Snow quality a little nicer as you get higher above the campground. Averaging 80cm of coverage at the toe of Roger’s Glacier (2350m south-east aspect) 10 of which fell last night. 

Temp at valley bottom(1300m): 4 degrees
Temp at campground (2100m): 0 degrees 
Temp at glacier (2350m): -2 degrees 

Summary: Keep biking.

items.title: Maddysparklez Megamind Mission
items.comments: Up to 30cm of well consolidated snow at 1800m with 5-10cm accumulating over 24hours. Graupel & some stellar stellars overnight. Lots of wind, not much transport at our elevation. Lower elevations lost snow coverage quickly. Paw pen 5cm tested by our dawg. 10/10 would recommend an early season mission.

items.title: Should have brought skates
items.comments:
6-8 inches of snow for the entire trail and even less above the lower lake.
Significant surface hoar forming throughout the day. Facets at ground level. Lower lake is frozen enough for skating but the area is not skiable yet.

items.comments: Ski touring across Wapta icefield and a summit of Rhondda on Nov. 13, 2026. Group of 3. Snow was variable with wind loading in areas, no shooting cracks or whumphing. Descended Rhondda then did a CT at the base of Mount Habel: CTM13 30cm down, RP. Included pics, At spot of the column test I lost 1 of my touring skis down the slope. Included a photo of area, if anyone finds it by chance my # is 403-431-2476. Will be going to peyto hut ~Nov 20th to look around for it. Also worth mentioning there were only a couple open crevasses around Rhondda and didn’t come across any hidden crevasses while traversing to and from bow hut from that area.

items.title: Bullmoose snow - thumbs down
items.comments: Height of snow 35-50 cm at treeline. 10 cm pretty good powder on top. The rest of the snowpack got really baked by this week’s warmup and it probably rained high up before the 10 cm snow. Wet and mushy, almost isothermic. We were sinking in almost down to ground. Would have been challenging skiing but we were on snowshoes.

items.title: For the love of the game.
items.comments: We took advantage of a break in the persistent cloudy conditions to get up high. Thin but very well settled snowpack at low elevations making for supportive travel. Extremely variable snowpack depths due to recent wind action above treeline but overall enough coverage to ski. Probing on the glacier revealed 150-200cm which, frankly, was a surprise. Skiing was decent but the wind from the previous day had crept into most places. We did not dig on the glacier due to extreme laziness but probing and pole probing gave the impression of a well settled, early winter snowpack up high. Overall, coverage is thin for November. Hopefully the storm track changes and we can get on with it out there.

items.title: Farnham season opener
items.comments: Still early season conditions in the Farnham zone but some slopes have certainly reached threshold! Overall the area had been hammered by wind and warm temps since the storm last weekend and we saw evidence of natural activity from the last week up to size 3. There is now a thin surface crust extending well into the alpine on NE aspects. We had a couple of small to medium whumpfs before remote triggering a size 1.5 avalanche while ascending the toe of the glacier. The slab failed on large facets just above glacier ice. We stuck to fairly mellow terrain afterwards. Overall the ski quality was not great. Breakable crust and/or windboard with a few pockets of soft that skied okay. Won’t be making the trek back until we start getting a fair bit more snow.

items.title: Shades of Beauty
items.comments:

Great ice quality, generally taking 13cm and 16cm screws.

Approach slopes are below threshold for avalanches.

The hiking trail is very slippery in places above the canyon (some fall hazard), microspikes would make the walk in way more comfortable.

items.title: Beauty Turns (w a side of early season faffing about)
items.comments:
Had a great day around Feather Peak this past Sunday. 

Though conditions below the alpine are still generally thin and variable, we found the snowpack had decent moisture content, which made it supportive under ski and allowed us to navigate through the lower elevations with only a reasonable amount of early season tom foolery.

As we moved up into more  exposed alpine terrain we found mixed snow conditions, including isolated wind slabs and increasing snowpack depth to a maximum of 160cm at 1600m. 

We observed a 1 to 2 day old naturally released slab avalanche (sz 1.5 - 2) around 1500m on a NE facing slope with crown depth of approx. 30-40cm, crown width of approx. 60m, that ran for about 100m.”

items.title: Powder - But at What Cost?
items.comments:
20cm of mushy garbage at the parking lot. Snowpack remained thin until ~1300m, then increased rapidly up to treeline at 1550 m. 

Significant winds Saturday night resulted in lots of snow transport and wind loading, with ~15 cm of new snow overnight at 1550 m. On Sunday we observed signs of storm slab formation along the uptrack, but no other signs of instability. 

HS was ~80 cm at treeline. Found some great powder turns on N–NE aspects.

Rapid warming throughout Sunday, with melting snow below ~1300 m. Fresh snow extended all the way to the parking lot, but was quickly turning to mush. Got thoroughly soaked on the bushwhack back to the car.

items.title: El classico Feather tour early season
items.comments:
It's early season, which means a small snowpack, open water and rocks are present. 
The sow was affected by wind from friday night. 
We saw some cracks and a group trigger a size 1 in a specific place. 
The snow cover in higher elevations is around 1.20m deep. 
At the road summit looks more 50cm.

items.title: Early Season Optimism
items.comments: With the weather station reading 16cm of fresh, this seemed like our best chance of getting some turns. The gully is still very rocky, the best skiing was actually below treeline, intersecting with the summer trail around 2050m. Lots of isolated reactive wind slabs in the alpine, shooting cracks. Didn't bother with a pit, average 15-20cm depth where it was actually skiable.

items.comments: Shooting cracks on isolated snow patch below the stem couloir.

items.title: Rocket Man
items.comments:
Approaching in the AM, HS 30cm, fist density, no obvious layers, boot pen to ground. Winds and precip picked up more than forecast in the PM. Sporadic heavier snowfall with wind transport triggered a natural sz 1.5, presumably windslab, which ran from above and terminated at the top of our approach slope. 

On our hurried descent, triggered another wind slab in relatively low density snow, crown height ~20cm, ran ~150m down a steep gulley. No involvement. Debris was ~40cm deep.

More shooting cracks in lower angle terrain.

items.title: Day 1 at Shames...game on...kind a.
items.comments: Zero snow in p lot.  Avoiding quicksand tower 2 to 4 is effortful.  Skins down on 2 cm's of crusty snow at tower 12.  5 to 10 cms at top chair.  20 ish cms top t.  Then big jump with 40 to 50 cms at prayer flags.  (1200 m's)  top crust of snow breaking  downish above T.  Reasonable fun turns down to 1000m's on PF's ridge run.  Heavy skinning at times on way up if tip dropped and full snow pack lifted.  Wet packy grains all the way to the moss.  No sluffy/slabby wet slides seen in back bowl.  Rode back down daintily to top of Geronimo.  Braver souls could go further.  Snowing  1-2 cms/hr at top tee when I left with wet flakes all the way to lodge.  Accumulating down to tower 5.  Cat track mud is super slick!  Almost went tits up 4 or 5 times on walk down.
